instruction.text: Find Thingvellir on the map of Iceland.

feedback.end: Although violence was important to the Vikings, this didn’t mean they were lawless. In AD 930, some Vikings moved to Iceland, and set up a government in Thingvellir called the Althing.

atoms.a: What do you think was the purpose of the Althing?

atoms.b: The Althing also voted on new Viking ((++laws stories)).
These laws were not written down but were instead remembered by someone called the law-speaker. The law-speaker’s job was to know all the laws and their ((++punishments treats)).
The law-speaker would stand on a spot ((++above inside)) the other men at the foot of Law Rock to recite the laws.

feedback.finish: Did you know that the Althing is still the national parliament of Iceland today — although, things have changed quite a lot since the Vikings!

atoms.a: If a Viking committed a violent crime, ...
atoms.sound: If a Viking committed a violent crime, they were declared an outlaw.

atoms.a: This meant that they had to live in the wilderness ...
atoms.b: and anyone was allowed to hunt them down and kill them.
atoms.sound: This meant that they had to live in the wilderness and anyone was allowed to hunt them down and kill them.

atoms.a: Lesser crimes or arguments could be settled ...
atoms.b: through an organised fight or duel, known as a holmgang.
atoms.sound: Lesser crimes or arguments could be settled through an organised fight or duel, known as a holmgang.

instruction.text: Alfred killed another person in his town. What would his punishment be?
What two things would happen to Alfred after being declared an outlaw?

b: ++People would be allowed to hunt him down.
He would be allowed to come to feasts.

instruction.text: Torsten and Bjørn are arguing over who owns a piece of land. How might they decide who owns the land?
What would happen if Torsten wins the fight?

b: No one would own the land.
